close_reason: Dropped pub on MAX_MERGE_PATCH_DEPTH constant — it's now pub(crate). Removed the export from crate-jmap-server/src/lib.rs. The constant is no longer part of the public API surface; consumers see the cap-exceeded behaviour via MergePatchError::DepthExceeded (introduced in bd:JMAP-wlip.1). Doc comment explicitly notes the workspace reserves the right to tighten the value (e.g. 32 → 16) without a major-version bump because the contract is the typed error, not the literal cap value. Public doc comments on json_merge_patch and MergePatchError::DepthExceeded that referenced the constant by intra-doc link are rewritten as plain text so rustdoc -D warnings stays clean.
description:
Scenario: the new pub const MAX_MERGE_PATCH_DEPTH (crate-jmap-server/src/helpers.rs:112) is re-exported from the crate root (lib.rs:23). A downstream extension *-server crate authors notes the constant and writes pre-validation: 'if patch_depth(patch) > MAX_MERGE_PATCH_DEPTH return SetError::InvalidPatch'. That code becomes the de facto API contract — and any future tightening of the constant (32 → 16 to harden further) silently changes the contract.

The constant is also exported alongside json_merge_patch, suggesting it is part of the public surface. But the only legitimate consumer of the constant is the test file in this crate. Once Issue JMAP-wlip.1 lands (json_merge_patch returns Result or bool), the constant becomes either internal implementation detail (caller doesn't need to know the value) or part of the contract (caller depth-validates before calling). It cannot be both.

Recommendation: defer this until JMAP-wlip.1's API shape lands. If JMAP-wlip.1 changes json_merge_patch to surface cap-exceeded as an error, drop the pub on MAX_MERGE_PATCH_DEPTH (keep the doc, remove the export). If it doesn't, document the constant's stability guarantee explicitly in its rustdoc.

Maintenance consequence: a consumer crate compiles against MAX_MERGE_PATCH_DEPTH = 32, the workspace tightens it to 16, and the consumer's pre-validation now rejects patches the server would accept (or vice versa). The drift is silent until a runtime mismatch.
title: MAX_MERGE_PATCH_DEPTH is exported with no actionable use for consumers
